title: Where the world's lightning actually strikes (percent of flashes)

source.name: Lightning Imaging Sensor / Optical Transient Detector (LIS-OTD) global lightning climatology

notes: NASA's LIS/OTD climatologies give a global mean land-to-ocean lightning flash ratio of about 10 to 1 - that is, roughly 90 percent of the world's lightning flashes happen over land and about 10 percent over ocean. Land heats quickly under the sun and drives strong convection; water warms slowly, so the air over it rises far less.
